definition: Used to introduce something that is different.
exampleSentence: I wanted to go to the concert, but the tickets were sold out.
We stayed inside because it was raining heavily all day.
The shop was closed, so we went to another one nearby.

definition: Used to say that something is true despite something else.
exampleSentence: Although it was cold, the children played outside all afternoon.

definition: Used to add a statement that is different from the one before.
exampleSentence: The hotel was expensive; however, the service was excellent.

definition: For that reason; as a result.
exampleSentence: The road is closed; therefore, we must take a different route.

definition: From a time in the past until now, or because.
exampleSentence: I have lived in this city since I was a child.
You will not pass the exam unless you study harder.

definition: During the time that something else happens.
exampleSentence: Someone called me while I was cooking dinner last night.
The library stays open until nine o'clock on weekdays.

definition: Used to compare two different facts.
exampleSentence: My brother loves the city, whereas I prefer the countryside.
Besides English, she speaks French and a little Arabic.
Save your work often; otherwise, you might lose everything.

definition: At the same time as something else.
exampleSentence: I will cook dinner; meanwhile, you can set the table.
The apartment is cheap; moreover, it is close to my office.
The software is free; furthermore, it works on every device.
Despite the rain, thousands of fans came to the concert.
The flight was delayed because of the snowstorm in Chicago.
The meeting was cancelled due to the manager's illness.

definition: In order to make something possible.
exampleSentence: Speak louder so that everyone in the room can hear you.

definition: In a way that suggests something is true.
exampleSentence: He talks as if he knows everything about computers.
I will go running tomorrow even if it rains.
Take an umbrella with you in case it rains later.

definition: Used to talk about two possible choices.
exampleSentence: I do not know whether he will come to the party.
Some fruits, for instance bananas, are rich in potassium.

definition: Used to say something again in a simpler way.
exampleSentence: The project failed; in other words, we lost all our money.
She speaks German as well as French and Spanish.

definition: Used with "but also" to add a second, stronger point.
exampleSentence: This app is not only fast but also very easy to use.

definition: Used to show a clear difference.
exampleSentence: Summers here are very hot; in contrast, the winters are mild.
In spite of the traffic, we arrived at the airport on time.

definition: Used to give a reason that should be remembered.
exampleSentence: Do not be too hard on him; after all, he is only a beginner.
A good teacher must be patient and, above all, kind to students.
The food was cold and the staff were rude; in short, it was a terrible evening.

definition: Used to start the final part of a speech or essay.
exampleSentence: In conclusion, regular exercise improves both health and mood.
To sum up, we need more time, more money and more people.
Cats sleep a lot during the day; similarly, owls rest until night.
My father was a doctor, and likewise my brother chose medicine.
The task was very difficult; nevertheless, we finished it on time.

definition: Used to say that the opposite is true.
exampleSentence: The movie was not boring; on the contrary, it was very exciting.

definition: As a result; in this way.
exampleSentence: The new design uses less power and thus saves money.
